name: What happens if there is old water damage behind the shower wall?

mainEntity.name: If demolition reveals hidden water damage behind the old shower, what usually needs to be repaired before the new walk-in shower goes in?
mainEntity.text: If demolition reveals hidden water damage behind the old shower, what usually needs to be repaired before the new walk-in shower goes in?

acceptedAnswer.text: If hidden water damage appears during demolition, the project usually needs a repair phase before the new shower can be built. Damaged drywall, backer board, insulation, framing, or subfloor materials must be removed until only sound structure remains. The leak source also has to be identified and corrected, whether it came from failed waterproofing, plumbing, or poor drainage. Installing a new shower over damaged material is a short-term fix that often leads to repeat problems. Depending on how far the moisture spread, the repair may include replacing framing members, drying the area, treating mold, and reworking the shower assembly from the studs or subfloor outward. This is one reason shower remodels can uncover more scope than expected. Homeowners should be prepared for the possibility that demolition will reveal issues that need to be addressed for the new shower to last.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hidden water damage usually means the damaged drywall, backer board, insulation, framing, or subfloor must be removed and rebuilt before the new shower is installed. The source of the leak must also be fixed so the problem does not return. Cosmetic repairs alone are not enough when structural moisture damage is present.
